resources.string: SocketFlip gives one app a clean, instant reconnect. Tap the floating button and the chosen app\'s open connections are closed by Android, so it reconnects straight away. Nothing else on the phone is touched and no traffic ever passes through SocketFlip.
Allow \"Display over other apps\" for SocketFlip, then come back and tap again.
SocketFlip needs VPN permission. Open SocketFlip and tap Show floating button.
The target app is not installed.
Choose a target app in SocketFlip first.
SocketFlip could not start its tunnel. Another VPN app may be set as Always-on.
SocketFlip could not start. Open SocketFlip and try again.
Floating button is on. Drag it anywhere; tap it to reconnect the target app.
Still reconnecting, try again in a few seconds.
Turn off Always-on VPN for SocketFlip

SocketFlip is set as your Always-on VPN with \"Block connections without VPN\". Its tunnel carries no traffic, so this cuts your phone off the internet. Tap here, then SocketFlip\'s gear icon, and turn both switches off.
SocketFlip is set as your Always-on VPN. It is not meant to be, and it stops your other VPN apps working. Tap here, then SocketFlip\'s gear icon, and turn Always-on VPN off.
SocketFlip is free and always will be. If it saves you time, a tip keeps it going.
Enjoying SocketFlip? It is free, open source and ad-free. If it has saved you some time, a small tip really helps.
Thank you! How would you like to give?

resources.string: You have version %1$s. SocketFlip never checks online by itself; this opens the latest release in your browser.
SocketFlip is free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 or later. You can read, change and share the source.
SocketFlip\'s tunnel has replaced your other VPN. Turn that VPN back on when you are done.
Android can only run one VPN at a time. If you carry on, your other VPN is switched off, and Android does not turn it back on by itself. Reopen that VPN app when you are done to reconnect it.
Everything SocketFlip needs, and whether your phone allows it. Tap Fix next to anything marked with a cross or an exclamation mark.

Not allowed, so the floating button cannot appear.
Off. The button still works, but you lose the Flip now and Stop actions and any warnings.
Not given yet, so a tap cannot reconnect anything.
Not checked, because another VPN is on and checking would switch it off. SocketFlip asks when you tap Show floating button.
Not exempted. This only matters on phones that close apps in the background.
SocketFlip has lost its VPN permission, most likely because another VPN app is set as Always-on. Turn Always-on off for that app in Android\'s VPN settings.
Another VPN app is set as Always-on

Android closed its VPN request before showing it, which it does when another VPN app is set as Always-on. SocketFlip cannot work while that is on. Open VPN settings, tap the gear next to that app and turn Always-on VPN off.
Android calls it a VPN, but SocketFlip only uses it to close the chosen app\'s connections. It carries no traffic and SocketFlip has no internet permission.
Another app is set as the Always-on VPN. If it also blocks connections without VPN, SocketFlip cannot start its tunnel.
Android does not let apps read this. If SocketFlip will not start, check that no app has Always-on VPN with Block connections without VPN.
Another VPN is on. A tap that brings SocketFlip\'s tunnel up will switch it off.
SocketFlip is allowed to run in the background.
Your phone may close the floating button in the background to save battery.

Phones from some makers close apps like SocketFlip in the background to save battery, and the floating button disappears. Allowing SocketFlip to run in the background stops that. It uses no battery while it is idle.
